name: Site timekeeping and biweekly payroll at a remote underground gold mine
summary: Every two weeks the mine pays about 280 hourly and staff employees who work 12-hour shifts on 14-days-on, 14-days-off rotations. Shift supervisors finalise crew timesheets with overtime, night and underground premiums and production bonus metres; the mine captain checks the bonus sheets; two payroll administrators check the hours against the rotation schedule, calculate bonuses in a spreadsheet, key everything into an outsourced payroll service and get the register approved before the service's cut-off. Late or unsigned timesheets from supervisors who have rotated off, bonus calculations and mid-period rate changes cause most of the corrections and the off-cycle payments after pay day.

baseline.org_archetype: A single-mine Canadian gold producer with about 280 people at a remote northern Ontario site on fly-in or drive-in rotations, an outsourced Canadian payroll service with site time entry, and a mid-market ERP.
baseline.notes: Describes 2019-2022 practice: daily paper or spreadsheet shift sheets, period timesheets scanned or emailed to payroll, bonus sheets in spreadsheets, payroll service web input, direct deposit, payroll journal posted to the ERP by import.

unit_of_work: one biweekly pay period for the site
trigger: The last shift of the two-week pay period ends and supervisors must hand in their crews' timesheets.
end_state: Employees are paid on pay day, source deductions are remitted to the CRA, and the payroll journal is posted and reconciled in the ERP.

volume.seasonality: Two pay periods in most months and three in two months a year. Work per period rises in the weeks of planned shutdowns (overtime) and around year-end (T4 preparation, benefit and rate changes on 1 January).

evidence.note: 26 biweekly pay periods a year (2.17 a month), matching the organisation file process_map entry.

systems.name: Payroll and timekeeping service (outsourced payroll with site time entry)
Shift reports, line-up boards and production tallies (paper and spreadsheets)
Gate access, camp booking and gold room access logs
Mid-market ERP for finance, purchasing, inventory and fixed assets
Shared drives and document library (procedures, permits, drawings)

steps.name: Underground supervisors finalise crew timesheets
steps.description: At the end of their last shift of the period, the underground shift supervisors on site total each crew member's hours from the daily shift sheets, mark overtime, night and underground premiums and absences, add the development metres and stope tonnes that drive the bonus, sign the timesheets and scan or email them to payroll.

error.defect_description: Missed overtime hours, wrong premium code or a crew member left off.

evidence.note: Four of the eight underground supervisors are on site in any two-week period under 14/14 rotation (organisation file). Time per supervisor is an estimate.

steps.name: Mill supervisors finalise crew timesheets
steps.description: The mill shift supervisors on site do the same for mill, crusher and gold room operators, using the mill shift log and line-up, and send the signed timesheets to payroll.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Maintenance supervisors finalise crew timesheets
steps.description: Maintenance supervisors total mechanics', electricians' and millwrights' hours, including call-outs and shutdown overtime, checking them against hours booked to work orders, and send the signed timesheets.

evidence.note: Maintenance timesheets are not linked to payroll in the organisation file; added here because 53 maintenance employees are paid hourly.

steps.name: Mine captain approves bonus sheets
steps.description: The mine captain compares each crew's claimed development metres and stope tonnes with the survey advance and the haulage tally, adjusts disputed claims and signs the bonus sheet.

control.basis: Site production bonus plan: bonus paid only on surveyed advance and measured tonnes

evidence.note: Production bonuses paid on development metres and tonnes are common at Canadian underground mines (organisation file process description); the check against survey is an estimate of common practice.

steps.name: HR sends employee changes for the period
steps.description: The site HR coordinator emails payroll the period's new hires with their signed offer and tax forms, terminations, promotions and rate changes approved under the compensation plan, and leave starts and returns.

error.defect_description: A rate change or termination is sent late or not at all.

evidence.note: Estimate; the organisation file sends new hires and the compensation plan into payroll.

steps.name: Collect timesheets and check completeness
steps.description: A payroll administrator downloads the scanned timesheets, ticks every name on the period's rotation roster against a timesheet, and lists missing, unsigned or illegible sheets.

evidence.note: Pay periods ending on a weekend are picked up by office-hours payroll staff on Monday; share of periods with missing sheets is an estimate.

steps.name: Chase missing or unsigned timesheets
steps.description: The administrator emails or phones the supervisors concerned; a supervisor who has rotated off may have to be reached at home, or the mine captain signs on their behalf.

evidence.note: Estimate; rotation means the supervisor who knows the hours is often off site.

steps.name: Check hours, overtime and premiums
steps.description: The administrators compare each employee's hours with the rotation schedule and the averaging agreement, check overtime and premium codes, and compare days claimed with gate and camp records where they differ.

control.basis: Ontario Employment Standards Act, 2000: hours of work, overtime and averaging agreements

evidence.note: Estimate. Overtime rules under a rotation hours-averaging arrangement are described from general knowledge of Ontario practice; the Employment Standards Act pages could not be opened.

steps.name: Calculate production bonuses
steps.description: An administrator enters the approved metres and tonnes into the bonus workbook, which applies the bonus rates by heading and crew, splits each crew's bonus by hours worked, and produces a bonus amount per employee.

error.defect_description: Wrong rate or crew split in the workbook.

evidence.note: Estimate; the organisation file names bonus calculations as a main cause of corrections.

steps.name: Enter employee changes
steps.description: The administrator sets up new hires (tax forms, banking, rate, cost centre), ends terminated employees and keys rate changes and leave in the payroll service.

error.defect_description: Wrong rate or banking detail keyed.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Key hours and bonuses into the payroll service
steps.description: The administrators key or import each employee's regular, overtime and premium hours by earnings code and cost centre, the bonus amounts and any one-off earnings and deductions into the payroll service's web input screens.

error.defect_description: Hours keyed to the wrong code or employee.

evidence.note: About 280 site employees with several earnings codes each; keying time is an estimate.

steps.name: Payroll service calculates preliminary register
steps.description: The payroll service calculates gross pay, tax, CPP, EI, union dues and benefit deductions and produces a preliminary register and variance report.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Second administrator reviews register
steps.description: The second payroll administrator, who did not key the batch, compares the register with last period by employee and department, looks at negative net pays, very large cheques and employees with no pay, and lists corrections.

control.basis: Payroll input reviewed by someone other than the person who keyed it

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Correct payroll entries
steps.description: The administrator who keyed the batch fixes the listed entries in the payroll service, asks the service to recalculate, and checks the changed employees again on the new register.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Site controller approves the register
steps.description: The site controller reviews the register summary, total gross and net pay by department against the previous period and the budget, asks about large movements and approves the payroll.

control.basis: Payroll approval by the site controller before release

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Commit payroll before the service cut-off
steps.description: The administrator submits the approved payroll in the payroll service before its processing cut-off, a few business days before pay day, and saves the confirmation.

evidence.note: Outsourced payroll services require submission a few business days before pay day for direct deposit; not checked against a provider's published schedule.

steps.name: Head office funds the payroll
steps.description: The treasury and tax manager checks the funding notice from the payroll service against the approved total and releases the transfer of net pay and remittances from the operating account.

control.basis: Bank mandate: funding released by head office treasury, not site payroll

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Pay day deposits and pay statements
steps.description: On pay day the payroll service deposits net pay into employees' bank accounts by direct deposit and publishes pay statements online, with the few remaining cheques mailed to site.

evidence.note: Pay day a few days after the payroll is committed; estimate.

steps.name: Answer employee pay queries
steps.description: In the days after pay day employees phone, email or come to the office about missing overtime, bonus amounts or deductions; the administrator checks the timesheet and bonus sheet and agrees whether an adjustment is due.

evidence.note: Estimate; most errors introduced earlier surface here as employee queries.

steps.name: Process off-cycle adjustment
steps.description: For large shortfalls the administrator runs an off-cycle payment in the payroll service; smaller ones are carried into the next period's input.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Remit source deductions to the CRA
steps.description: The payroll service remits the income tax, CPP and EI withheld and the employer's share to the CRA for the remitting period that contains pay day. With withholdings well above C$100,000 a month the company is a threshold 2 accelerated remitter, so each remittance is due the third working day after the 7th, 14th, 21st or last day of the month.

control.basis: Income Tax Regulations s.108 and CRA remitting rules for threshold 2 accelerated remitters

evidence.note: Due dates and the C$100,000 threshold are from the CRA pages. The company's average monthly withholding (about C$600,000-900,000 for roughly C$30 million of annual site payroll) is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Post payroll journal and labour distribution
steps.description: The administrator exports the payroll journal from the service, maps earnings and deductions to ERP accounts and labour cost by department and cost centre, imports it into the ERP and posts it.

error.defect_description: Labour charged to the wrong department or capital project.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Reconcile payroll accounts
steps.description: A site accountant reconciles the payroll clearing, source deduction and benefit payable accounts against the register, the funding transfer and the remittance, and clears or follows up differences.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: monthly reconciliation of payroll liability accounts

evidence.note: Estimate.

exceptions.name: Missing or unsigned timesheets
exceptions.description: One or more supervisors have rotated off without sending signed timesheets.

exceptions.name: Register corrections
exceptions.description: Second review finds keying or bonus errors that are fixed before approval.

exceptions.name: Off-cycle payment
exceptions.description: An employee is short-paid by enough to need an off-cycle payment.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the end of the pay period to the payroll journal posted and reconciled
benchmarks.population: Biweekly site payroll with an outsourced service, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Author's estimate: pay day about six days after period end, remittance within days of pay day, journal and reconciliation in the following week.

benchmarks.unit: working days after the end of each quarter-month remitting period

pain_points.description: Supervisors on 14/14 rotation leave site before timesheets are signed, so payroll chases them at home.

evidence.note: Follows from the organisation file shift patterns; estimate.

pain_points.description: Bonus metres are tallied by hand, checked against survey and calculated in a spreadsheet, the main source of pay errors and queries.

evidence.note: Organisation file process description names bonus calculations as the main cause of corrections.

pain_points.description: Hours and bonuses are re-keyed from paper or scanned timesheets into the payroll service.

evidence.note: Estimate of 2019-2022 practice at single-mine producers.

sources.title: When to remit (pay): remitting due dates for source deductions
sources.supports: Threshold 2 accelerated remitters remit up to four times a month (periods 1-7, 8-14, 15-21, 22-end), due the third working day after each period ends; threshold 1 remits twice a month.

sources.title: Types of remitters
sources.supports: Threshold 2 accelerated remitter status applies when the average monthly withholding amount two calendar years earlier was $100,000 or more; remitter type is not related to pay periods.

assumptions: The case is one biweekly pay period for the site's hourly and staff employees. Head office staff in Toronto are assumed to be paid by the same payroll service but set up by head office; they are not stepped through here.
Daily time recording during the period is part of the shift control processes; this file starts when the period ends.

The organisation file triggers payroll only from mine shift control and the mill. Maintenance timesheets are added here through mnt-work-planning, the nearest maintenance process in the organisation file, because about 53 maintenance employees are paid hourly. HSE, warehouse, camp and administration timesheets also arrive but are small.

Roles added beyond the organisation file's list for this process (payroll-admin, site-controller, ug-shift-supervisor): mill-shift-supervisor, maint-supervisor, mine-captain, hr-coordinator, treasury-tax-manager and site-accountant, all existing roles.

Staffing: per-period work in this file implies about 0.5-0.6 FTE of payroll administrator time; the organisation file has 2 administrators. The difference is daily timekeeping support, benefits, records of employment, WSIB and Employer Health Tax filings and year-end slips, which are outside this per-period flow.

Remitter type: about C$30 million of annual site payroll gives withholdings far above the CRA's C$100,000 monthly threshold, so the company is a threshold 2 accelerated remitter (cra-types, cra-due). The amount is an estimate.
Pay day falls about six calendar days after period end; this lag and the payroll service cut-off are estimates of common Canadian practice, not taken from a provider's published schedule.

The simulated median of about 11.5 days is slightly above the 10-day estimate because the validator adds the payroll administrators' 30 or so hands-on hours per period end to end as elapsed time, whereas in practice two administrators split them over two working days.
Loaded costs are taken from the organisation file.
